Prepare a cohort survey design

Source: R/design.R
nis_design.Rd

Collects cohort rows and one zero-domain placeholder per hospital-year with no cohort discharges, then builds a nested NIS survey design. The placeholder-row method is experimental and is gated against a full-data design. After this function returns, filter() may only narrow the declared cohort; it cannot define a new cohort. Hospital geography columns are optional. Hospital and stratum identifiers are scoped by year (YEAR + HOSP_NIS and YEAR + NIS_STRATUM), because HCUP reassigns hospital numbers annually and 2023 stratum codes are sequential. Costs and charges use TOTCHG only, unless charges names another column such as TOTCHG_2023; nothing is coalesced silently, because the 2023 field is not comparable to earlier-year TOTCHG. The 2023 layout facts (TOTCHG_2023, removed HOSP_REGION and HOSP_DIVISION, sequential strata) are UNVERIFIED against official HCUP 2023 documentation and real 2023 data.

Usage

nis_design(
  .data,
  cohort,
  keep,
  annualize = FALSE,
  dollars = NULL,
  charges = "TOTCHG"
)

Arguments

.data

Lazy DuckDB query or data frame.

cohort

Logical data-masked cohort expression. Missing values are counted and treated as outside the cohort. Only valid-design discharges are counted.

keep

Tidyselect expression naming analysis columns to collect.

annualize

Divide discharge weights by the number of distinct YEAR values among valid-design discharges. A year counts as one whole year however much of it is present, so a partial-year era such as the ICD-10 fourth quarter of 2015 counts the same as a full year, and a year with no cohort discharges still counts. When DQTR is present, a warning identifies years where the valid-design data has fewer than four quarters. A separate warning identifies a cohort limited to the ICD-9 (Q1-Q3) or ICD-10 (Q4) part of 2015. Exclude partial years or use annualize = FALSE and apply a suitable fractional-year factor with nis_reweight() if you need a different convention.

dollars

Optional reference dollar year for adjusted costs and charges. When supplied, keep CCR_NIS and the charges column.

charges

Name of the total-charge column used for adjusted costs and charges. Defaults to "TOTCHG". Use "TOTCHG_2023" for 2023-only analyses, or build a pooled column explicitly with dplyr::mutate(TOTCHG = dplyr::coalesce(TOTCHG_2023, TOTCHG)) before calling; either choice mixes charge definitions across years.

Value

A filtered srvyr::tbl_svy survey design.

Invalid design fields

Discharges whose YEAR, HOSP_NIS, NIS_STRATUM, or DISCWT is missing, non-finite, or not positive are excluded before the cohort is applied. HCUP specifies DISCWT as the discharge weight, NIS_STRATUM as the stratum, and HOSP_NIS as the hospital cluster (variance guidance; 2017 NIS introduction); HCUP also documents missing and invalid coding conventions (coding conventions). Records with invalid values cannot be placed in the documented design as supplied. Exclusion is not a claim that these records have zero population weight or that estimates are unbiased. Report the excluded count and affected fields, and consider whether conclusions could depend on them. The returned design has a nis_excluded attribute containing aggregate total, by_field, and by_year counts; by_year includes years with exclusions when the year is itself valid. A discharge can fail more than one field.

The query is scanned twice for design validation and cohort collection. When annualizing and DQTR is present, quarter coverage requires an additional summary scan. The cohort expression is evaluated once over the full data.

See also

Survey design and weighting.

Other survey-design: nis_reweight()

Examples

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpjI8hwc/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).

#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpjI8hwc/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpjI8hwc/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
design <- nis_design(
  nis,
  cohort = heart_failure & AGE >= 50,
  keep = c(AGE, FEMALE, TOTCHG, CCR_NIS),
  dollars = 2024
)
#> Warning: Missing values are always removed in SQL aggregation functions.
#> Use `na.rm = TRUE` to silence this warning
#> This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.
#> Cohort: 72 discharges; weighted N 83.2; 18 hospitals across 2 years.
srvyr::summarise(
  design,
  discharges = srvyr::survey_total(),
  mean_age = srvyr::survey_mean(AGE)
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   discharges discharges_se mean_age mean_age_se
#>        <dbl>         <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
